<description>
Several numeric configuration options now reject values that are out of range instead of silently wrapping or inverting. Previously a negative value could disable the intended limit entirely.

  - `-dbbatchsize` and `-dbcrashratio` must be non-negative. A negative `-dbbatchsize` wrapped to a huge value and disabled batch flushing, so a reindex could hold an unbounded batch in memory.
  - `-limitclustersize`, `-limitancestorcount`, `-limitdescendantcount`, `-mempoolexpiry`, `-datacarriersize`, `-maxsendbuffer`, `-maxreceivebuffer`, `-bantime`, `-bytespersigop` and `-maxtipage` must be non-negative.
  - `-limitclustercount` must be between 1 and 64.
  - `-timeout` must be positive. It previously fell back to the default silently, unlike the analogous `-peertimeout`, which already errored.

  Zero remains valid wherever it already meant "disabled": `-dbbatchsize=0`,
  `-limitclustersize=0`, `-datacarriersize=0`, `-mempoolexpiry=0`,
  `-maxtipage=0`, `-bytespersigop=0`, `-maxsendbuffer=0`,
  `-maxreceivebuffer=0` and `-bantime=0`.

- The `-help` output for `-bytespersigop`, `-datacarriersize`, `-dbbatchsize`, `-stopatheight` and `-checkblockindex` now shows the `=<n>` placeholder for their value, matching how they are actually parsed.
</description>
